calls.body: On the power play, Detroit is near the top of the league, but St. Louis is one of the worst. Every penalty the Blues take could cost them.

surprises.head: St. Louis took away the good looks
surprises.body: St. Louis is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Detroit’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 5.9% against St. Louis) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: The Blues get past the Red Wings
paras: Andrew Copp opened the scoring for the Red Wings with 13 seconds left in the first. Pius Suter scored his 100th NHL goal just 37 seconds into the second to tie it 1-1. Justin Barron put the Blues ahead for good just under two minutes later, and Ross Johnston and Andreas Englund dropped the gloves midway through the period. Jimmy Snuggerud made it 3-1 for the Blues with just over four minutes left, and that one stood up as the winner. With the goalie pulled and a little over a minute left, Moritz Seider cut St. Louis’ lead to 3-2, but the Blues held on.

The Blues had the better of the chances, outshooting the Red Wings 32-21 at 5-on-5. Joel Hofer made 29 saves for the Blues, and John Gibson stopped 30 of 33 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Dylan Holloway, by our Swing measure. The Blues moved to 8-8-2, seventh in the Central, while the Wings fell to 7-9-3, still last in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Blues won for the first time in four games.
